phases.subject: compiler-design

focus.text: LR family: LR(0) items, SLR vs LALR vs CLR, SR/RR conflicts, counting states
LL(1): FIRST/FOLLOW, parse table, is it LL(1)?
Liveness analysis, basic blocks, control-flow graphs
SDT: S- vs L-attributed, evaluate what an SDT prints
Three-address code, DAG and common subexpressions, constant propagation

phases.title: Programming & Data Structures
phases.subject: programming-ds

focus.text: C output tracing: pointers, arrays, strings, recursion, static variables, scope
Trees: BST, AVL rotations and height bounds, rebuild from traversals
Heaps: build-heap, insert/delete, array positions
Hashing: linear/quadratic probing, chaining, expected probes
Stacks and queues: infix to postfix, evaluation, queue from stacks; linked lists

skip: Graph representation in depth (Algorithms covers it)
phases.note: A few C-output PYQs every day of this block.

phases.title: Algorithms
phases.subject: algorithms

focus.text: Graphs: BFS/DFS edge types and timings, Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, MST (Prim, Kruskal)
Asymptotics and recurrences: master theorem, recursion tree
DP: LCS, matrix-chain, 0/1 knapsack, Floyd–Warshall
Sorting: best/worst cases, comparisons, stability; quick and merge sort analysis
Greedy: Huffman, activity selection, fractional knapsack

skip: Amortised analysis beyond the basic idea
phases.note: Dijkstra and Bellman-Ford come back in CN routing.

focus.text: Number representation: 2's complement range and overflow, IEEE 754 single precision
K-maps: minimal SOP, prime and essential prime implicants, don't-cares
Counters: mod-N, ripple vs synchronous, trace the sequence
MUX as a function, decoders, adders and carry-lookahead delay
Flip-flops: characteristic tables and conversions
Cache: mapping, tag/index/offset bits, hit ratio, AMAT, write-back vs write-through
Pipelining: speedup, CPI with stalls, hazards, forwarding, branch penalty
Instruction formats and addressing modes (opcode bit counting)
I/O: interrupts, DMA burst vs cycle stealing, % of CPU time
Main memory and interleaving
IPv4, CIDR, subnetting, longest prefix match
TCP: congestion window (slow start, AIMD, threshold), flow control, sequence numbers
Sliding window: stop-and-wait, Go-Back-N, Selective Repeat efficiency and sequence bits
Data link: CRC, CSMA/CD minimum frame size, Ethernet
Routing: distance vector, link state; IP fragmentation; ARP, DHCP, ICMP, NAT

phases.title: Maths, the scoring parts
phases.subject: discrete-maths

focus.text: Propositional and first-order logic: equivalence, validity, English to quantifiers
Linear algebra: rank, determinant, eigenvalue shortcuts, when a system has solutions
Sets, relations, functions: counting relations, equivalence relations, posets
Graph theory: degree sum, connectivity, planar graphs, colouring, matching
Probability: conditional, Bayes, expectation; binomial, Poisson, uniform
Counting: permutations, combinations, pigeonhole, inclusion–exclusion

phases.note: Aim for 8–10 of these marks. The skipped parts cost about 3–5.

focus.text: Full-length mock (65 Qs, 3 h) every Mon, Wed, Fri at exam time
Morning after: analyse, fix notes, re-solve PYQs of topics under 60%
Other days: revise subjects, heaviest first (PDS, COA, OS, CN, TOC)

Formula sheets and GATE traps only, no new topics
